subject: Biotechnology
title: Designer Babies and Enhancement
description: A fast breakdown of Designer Babies and Enhancement for builders.

hook.text: Cure disease or enhance intelligence? The line between therapy and enhancement blurs as gene editing advances.

buildup.text: Editing out sickle cell disease is therapy — editing for taller height or higher IQ crosses into enhancement territory.

discovery.text: Intelligence involves thousands of genes each with tiny effects — designer babies are scientifically impractical today.

twist.text: If enhancement becomes possible, only the wealthy could afford it — genetic inequality could become permanent and heritable.

climax.text: The Nuffield Council said germline editing might be ethical if it promotes welfare and does not increase inequality.

punchline.text: Cure or upgrade? Society must decide before the technology decides for us.

quiz.question: Why are designer babies with enhanced intelligence currently impractical?
options: CRISPR cannot edit genes related to brain function
Intelligence involves thousands of genes with tiny individual effects, making meaningful enhancement scientifically unfeasible
No country allows research on genes related to intelligence

details.summary: Designer babies refers to the concept of using genetic engineering to select or modify traits in human embryos beyond disease prevention, potentially including intelligence, physical appearance, or athletic ability. This possibility raises fundamental questions about equality and human identity.
details.whyItMatters: The line between treating genetic disease and enhancing human traits is ethically blurry. If genetic enhancement becomes possible, access could create biological inequality between those who can afford it and those who cannot.
takeaways: Germline editing could theoretically modify heritable traits in embryos
Most complex traits involve hundreds of genes with unpredictable interactions
International consensus currently prohibits heritable human genome editing

faq.question: Could parents really choose their child's intelligence or appearance?
faq.answer: Not with current technology. Traits like intelligence involve thousands of gene variants each contributing tiny effects, plus massive environmental influence. Editing for these traits is scientifically impractical and would risk unpredictable side effects.

faq.question: Why do most countries ban heritable human genome editing?
faq.answer: Changes to embryo DNA are passed to all future generations, making mistakes permanent and irreversible. Unknown long-term effects, consent issues for future people, and the risk of creating genetic inequality led to near-universal international prohibition.
